original_question: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a set S of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is G, where vertices correspond to segment endpoints and two endpoints are adjacent when the segment joining them avoids all segments of S, with the two endpoints of each original segment also adjacent.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 12 in Section 3.1 (Visibility Graphs: Recognition, Characterization, and Reconstruction): given a graph in adjacency matrix form, determine whether it is the segment visibility graph of a set of disjoint segments in the plane.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right recognition problem, the adjacency-matrix input, the requirement that the realizing objects are pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane, the fact that vertices correspond to segment endpoints rather than to whole segments, and the extra adjacency between the two endpoints of each original segment.
missing_details: The paper's object is specifically the segment visibility graph (also called the segment endpoint visibility graph) of a finite set S of disjoint line segments in the plane.
The vertex set must be in bijection with the full endpoint set P of S; equivalently, if S has m segments then the graph has exactly 2m vertices.
For endpoints p and q belonging to distinct segments, adjacency is defined by geometric visibility: the straight segment joining p and q must meet no segment of S except possibly at p and q.

The paper makes the visibility convention stricter than your wording suggests: the joining segment is not allowed to pass through any other endpoint of S, and it is not allowed to graze along any segment of S.
The adjacency between the two endpoints of the same segment is an additional rule, not a consequence of the ordinary visibility test.
To make the question fully stand-alone, it should say explicitly that the task is recognition—whether such a segment set exists for the given graph—rather than characterization or reconstruction.
refined_question: Given a finite graph G in adjacency-matrix form, decide whether there exists a finite set S = {s_1, ..., s_m} of pairwise disjoint line segments in the Euclidean plane, with endpoint set P = {a_1, b_1, ..., a_m, b_m}, such that G is exactly the segment visibility graph of S: V(G) is in bijection with P; for endpoints p,q in P that belong to distinct segments, pq is an edge of G if and only if the straight segment joining p and q meets no segment of S except possibly at p and q (in particular, it does not pass through any other endpoint and does not graze along any segment of S); and for each i, the two endpoints a_i and b_i of s_i are adjacent in G.
justification: The draft clearly targets the segment-visibility recognition problem, not the point-visibility problems in Section 2. Section 1 gives the operative definition of a segment visibility graph: vertices are endpoints of disjoint segments, endpoint pairs on different segments are adjacent when joined by an unobstructed straight segment under the paper's no-passing-through-endpoints/no-grazing convention, and each original segment contributes an edge between its own endpoints. Section 3.1 then states exactly the corresponding recognition question as Open Problem 12. The refined version therefore stays at precisely that scope and merely folds the Section 1 definitions into the official formulation so that the question is fully stand-alone.
